content:
We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

Structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH (anilide). So overall three disconnections suggested: 1) amide formation between carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (maybe 4-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl group attached to phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid side chain.

Thus retrosynthetic steps:

Step 1 (last forward): amide coupling: carboxylic acid (trans-α,β-unsaturated acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> amide.

So retrosynthetic disconnection: target -> amide precursor: C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (the unsaturated amide) and the sulfonyl phenyl part? Wait the amide is attached to the phenyl ring that also has sulfonamide. Actually the target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (the second phenyl). The amide is attached to that phenyl via the carbonyl attached to the same phenyl? Let's examine: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (c2) has a substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH. So the amide carbonyl is attached to the phenyl via the carbonyl carbon (C=O) attached to the phenyl? Actually the SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)N... The carbonyl carbon is attached to the phenyl via the carbonyl carbon? The pattern: phenyl - C(=O)N... preceded by /C=C/. So the phenyl is attached to the alkene carbon (beta carbon) of the unsaturated acid? Wait typical cinnamoyl: Ph-CH=CH-CO-... So the phenyl attaches to the carbonyl carbon? Actually cinnamoyl: Ph-CH=CH-CO- . So the phenyl is attached to the carbonyl carbon? No, the carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene carbon (beta). So the phenyl is attached to the carbonyl carbon? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N...)cc2. The substituent is /C=C/C(=O)N... attached to the phenyl at the carbon of the alkene (the first carbon of the double bond). So the phenyl is attached to the alkene carbon (alpha). So the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via the alkene carbon.

Thus step 1: amide formation between unsaturated acid (C=CC(=O)O) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via the alkene carbon; that phenyl is the same phenyl (c2). So the unsaturated acid precursor is: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 (cinnamic acid attached to phenyl). Then amide coupling with aniline gives target after also sulfonamide formation.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target -> disconnection 1: break amide bond between carbonyl and aniline N. Precursors: (A) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 (cinnamic acid phenyl) and (B) aniline (c3ccccc3N). Also sulfonamide remains attached to phenyl (c2) with sulfonyl group attached to p-tolyl amine.

Step 2: break sulfonamide bond between sulfonyl group and p-tolyl amine. Precursors: (C) p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and (D) sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl-sulfonyl chloride where phenyl has the cinnamic acid substituent: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2. So we need that sulfonyl chloride.

Step 3: formation of cinnamic acid via Doebner modification: from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) to give c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We don't have IDs; we can search for templates matching criteria.

Step 1: amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid? The acid is aliphatic? It's unsaturated acid attached to aromatic, but still aliphatic carboxylic acid. functional_groups_formed: amide. Let's search.
